chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'The marketplace of the Muslims is like their mosque; whoever arrives first at a spot is more entitled to it until evening, and he did not charge rent for the shops of the marketplace.'

key_terms.مَسْجِدِهِمْ: Their mosques (used metaphorically for public domain)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling regarding priority rights and rent in public marketplaces?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) attributes a practical economic policy to Imam Ali (AS), establishing the marketplace as a public domain (sadaqah) where priority is granted to the first occupier until evening. The exemption from rent (kira') underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on removing barriers to trade and ensuring equitable access for merchants, reflecting the concept of 'urf' (customary practice) in early Islamic jurisprudence.
